definition: A prompt formulated around explicit guiding principles used to instruct a model (or an evaluator model) on how to critique or judge outputs according to those principles.
details: Constitutional prompts operationalize written principles (as in Constitutional AI) into concrete instructions a model can use for self-critique or evaluation, forming a building block of principle-based training pipelines.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. The idea is simple: before something powerful is let loose, someone checks that it will not do real harm to real people. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. That deliberate caution is Constitutional Prompt.
